Hi Sara — great to meet you and appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP workbook (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) with milestones and a recommended sizing exercise. High-level summary below:

Pilot recommendation (goal: validate latency, cold-start behavior, and routing policies)
- Start: 6 H100-equivalent GPUs (baseline) with autoscale burst to 12 GPUs for peak testing. This generally covers 15–25 qps with headroom for model size up to ~70B.
- Alternative (cost-first): 8xA100-80GB with heavier batching; expect slightly higher 95th latency.

Lead time estimates (typical):
- Hosted / Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): 4–8 weeks from signed commitment to green traffic for a standard region deploy (shorter if PO + SSO + billing cleared).
- Redwood Private (VPC + customer-managed infra) or on-prem: 8–14 weeks typically — includes network peering, KMS integration, and security acceptance testing.

Milestones in the attached MAP (dates are placeholders; we can tighten):
1) Eval kickoff (week 0) — test dataset, acceptance thresholds, key prompt sets.
2) Pilot deployment (week 1–2) — put the pilot pool behind our routing layer.
3) Performance run / quality sign-off (week 2–4).
4) Procurement & legal (parallel) — finalize billing/commitment / DocuSign.
5) Activation & scale (post-sign) — Dedicated: ~4–8w, Private: ~8–14w.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

If you can share a target go-live window (or latest date when you’d need Dedicated vs Private online) we’ll mark hard checkpoints. I’ll loop in Marissa for commercial cadence and Soojin for acceptance criteria and SOC2 evidence.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Michael / Marissa — quick notes from infra/solutions POV:

- Sizing: start with 6 H100s is reasonable for a performance-first pilot if model ~35B and you want consistent 95th percentile < 200ms for generation. Recommend autoscale policy: burst to 12 for 30-minute windows; keep continuous concurrency throttles to avoid runaway cost.
- Alternative: 8xA100-80GB works if they prioritize unit cost; expect 15–25% slower p95 on long sequences.
- Private/on-prem lead time: realistically plan 10–16 weeks for an enterprise on-prem install that includes site survey, rack/cooling validation, KMS/HSM integration (customer IT often adds 2–4 weeks for certs), and SOC/pen-test windows. If customer uses our VPC private-hosted option (no hardware on site) it’s closer to the Dedicated cadence but still needs network peering and IP allowlisting (6–10 weeks).
- SOC2 artifacts: attaching a short bundle for procurement. We should include a one-page attestation summary in the MAP and point procurement to the secure evidence bundle.

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-stub.zip (zip)

I can draft a technical appendix for the MAP with acceptance tests (latency p95 targets, KV cache validation, cold start test plan). If they want to compress Dedicated activation to 4 weeks we should require: PO within 7 days, cleared billing, and a dedicated onboarding SRE window (2 full-time days).

—Soojin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
